messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT P1 — elevated 99th latency and OOM churn on continuous-batcher (prod-west). Auto-created incident channel and paged eng-oncall @here.

maya: noticing batch accumulator keeps growing even when qdepth drops. memory per-batcher process climbing from 1.2GB -> 14GB in ~8m on gpunode-13.

sam: seeing repeated CUDA page fault spikes in kernel logs, followed by container restarts. dmesg shows GPU page fault and tdr-like resets.

maya: logs (tail):
```
[2026-03-15T12:04:22Z] continuous_batcher.cpp:482 alloc_kv_cache(): kv_cache_size=256MB -> 1.2GB
[2026-03-15T12:05:10Z] runtime_gpu.cpp:133 cuda_page_fault: 0x3: map_invalid
[2026-03-15T12:06:05Z] supervisor: restarting container continuous-batcher (exit 137)
```

leon: could be the new prefetch/pipeline refactor — accumulator isn't capping when concurrency drops. I've seen a livelock where prefetch keeps attaching new batches to the accumulator while eviction never runs.

jia: confirmed a spike in prefix cache growth at the same timestamps in graphite: KV-prefetch-entries went from 120k -> 1.2M. Correlates with batch_accumulator.size metric.

maya: customer impact: several SLAs showing 10x tail latency for model text-generation routes; some requests 30s+. A subset of customers in prod-west reporting timeouts.

sam: mitigation plan suggestion (live):
- stop-prefetch on nodes showing growth
- reduce continuous_batcher.max_accumulation to 8
- temporarily route critical customers to standby region (prod-east)

leon: agree. Quick commands to do a rolling fix on the cluster:
```bash
# mark node unschedulable and drain non-critical pods
kubectl cordon gpunode-13
kubectl drain gpunode-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force

# patch deployment to lower accumulation at runtime (env var guard)
kubectl -n infra patch deployment continuous-batcher -p '\n{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"containers": [{"name":"continuous-batcher","env": [{"name":"CB_MAX_ACCUM","value":"8"}] }]}}}}'
```

maya: applying patch now to prod-west one-by-one, starting with non-primary AZ. I'll also instruct traffic router to prefer prod-east for critical customers.

deploy-bot: Started rollout of patched continuous-batcher to prod-west (deploy/continuous-batcher) — rollout id r-20260315-01.

sam: while rollout proceeds, we should avoid killing containers aggressively — restarts lose KV cache and make latency worse for warm customers. Prefer node cordon + new pods on patched config.

ops-bot: Routing change applied: route-policy continuous-batcher -> prefer prod-east for customer set [acme-corp, beta-suite].

jia: monitoring notes: set an alert to suspend automated prefetch for 10m if kv_prefetch_entries > 250k and batch_accumulator.size > 1000. That will give time to patch and avoid runaway growth.

maya: Quick check: anyone seeing OOM killer on host instead of container? Host logs show oom_killer not triggered; it's process exit 137 inside container right after CUDA page fault.

leon: sounds like GPU pagefault is cascading: as accumulator grows, CUDA allocations fail, drivers trigger reset, containers crash. Root cause likely logic bug that doesn't respect backpressure signals.

sam: temporary workaround on affected nodes: set environment var `RD_BATCHER_PREFETCH=false` and lower `RD_BATCHER_PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=1` to prevent new prefetch jobs.

maya: patch applied to two nodes. I'm watching metrics. batch_accumulator.size trending down on those AZs. tail latency improving from 28s -> 2.3s for most customers.

jia: creating short postmortem checklist and recording timeline. Need full RCA next.

leon: To eng-runtime: please capture core/driver logs from gpunode-13 (dmesg, nvidia-smi --query, container logs) and preserve pod images for debugging (don't gc).

maya: drafted customer message for CS to send (feel free to trim):
"We experienced elevated tail latency and intermittent failures for text-generation in prod-west starting ~12:04 UTC due to an internal continuous-batcher bug that caused GPU page faults and container restarts. Mitigation applied — traffic shifted and batcher config patched. We're investigating root cause and will follow up."

sam: I'm handing over to eng-runtime for deeper investigation — marking as active incident and creating ticket RT-6243 for driver/interactions + prefetch logic regression.

leon: follow-ups (todo):
- add stricter invariants to accumulator (hard cap + eviction fairness)
- add signal path for prefetch to back off on pagefaults
- unit/integration tests that simulate eviction starvation
- post-deploy ramp for prefetch feature flags

maya: thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread open for the handoff. leon/jia/sam — please coordinate on RCA and postmortem doc.

oncall-bot: Incident channel created: #incident-1718001234-batcher-livelock. Incident severity P1 -> acknowledged.

maya: handing to eng-runtime now — tagging @leon and @sam for the on-call rotation.

leon: taking it. will follow up with timelines and next steps in the incident doc.

sam: ack, staying on until root cause confirmed.

ops-bot: Note: scheduled maintenance window for gpunode-13 tomorrow 02:00 UTC; ensure we capture required artifacts before then.

maya: last update before handing off: tail latency largely normalized for most customers, a few long tails remain but are being routed east. continuing monitoring.

leon: last note — avoid full `pkill` on continuous-batcher unless instructed; prefer controlled rollout to keep warm caches where possible.
